verdict.rationale: Logseq documents an official quickCapture flow via its logseq:// protocol. It can be added as a browser bookmark and uses a template that records the captured text with its source URL, so it is a real first-party capture flow from the browser. However, the docs scope it to "short text and links": there is no evidence of full-page or article clipping, and no browser highlight capture. The CORS-enabled local HTTP API and third-party plugins are only developer building blocks, so they earn no credit here. missing for 10: full web page/article clipping, browser highlight capture, an official clipper extension, and hands-on corroboration of the bookmarklet flow.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can clip web pages, articles, and highlights from my browser straight into my notes with an official clipper or capture flow

citations.quote: Quick capture for short text and links. Can be added as a bookmark link to modern browser or opened from command line shell
Logseq provides a protocol `logseq://` to allow third party applications to invoke actions within Logseq.
